newsitem.title: GERMANY: Germany eyes trade prospects from telecoms deal.
newsitem.headline: Germany eyes trade prospects from telecoms deal.

text.p: The German government took some credit on Monday for a landmark agreement at the weekend to open the $600 billion global telecommunications market to competition.
"We implemented one of the world's most liberal telecommunications laws last year and with our law we helped to drive this process," a spokesman for Post and Telecommunications Ministry said.
Deutsche Telekom AG, Germany's dominant telecoms player that enjoys a monopoly on basic phone services until 1998, welcomed the deal and said it would enhance global competition.
"It will be easier to offer international customers services from one hand and to follow our customers wherever they go around the world," a company spokesman said.
"Now we expect that we will be able to find competitive conditions in other markets in the world like those that have been established in Germany and Europe," he added.
Deutsche Telekom was partially privatised last year.

Most countries in the European Union will drop the last barriers to full competition in telecommunications on January 1, 1998. Some segments of the industry are already open to competition, such as data services, mobile communications and cable television.

The World Trade Organisation (WTO) accord on telecommunications was signed by 68 countries on Saturday in Geneva after to more than three years of on-off negotiations to bring free trade principles to the booming telecoms sector.

World leaders heralded the accord, which covers 93 percent of the global telecommunications market, as a major victory for free trade that will benefit consumers, create jobs and bring the information revolution to the farthest reaches of the globe.
